topics.topic: Final run status when an execution is refused_by_owner
questions: Must a run containing a refused_by_owner execution end with status refused or, because not every node succeeded or was skipped_by_guard, with status failed?
When a refused_by_owner execution exists and nothing waits, must the run end refused or failed, or must the latter rule explicitly exclude refused_by_owner?

judgement.why: This is the same question on unchanged text as P10.

precedent.topic: Final run status when an execution is refused_by_owner
quotes: If any NodeExecution of the run is refused_by_owner it reaches nothing and ends the run refused.
precedent.why: The terminal status is explicitly refused.

topics.topic: How answer_request handles handler exceptions translated to internal_error
questions: Must a handler exception translated as internal_error propagate unchanged to serve_kernel, or be returned by answer_request as a tools/call result with isError true?
Must a handler exception translated as internal_error propagate unchanged to serve_kernel, or must it be returned by answer_request as an isError tool result like every translated handler exception?

quotes: MUST call the handler of the named operation, whose name is handle_ followed by the operation name — exactly one of handle_accept_binding, handle_activate_flow_version, handle_add_trial_case, handle_cancel_run, handle_capture_failed_execution, handle_compose_flow_version, handle_decide_effect_approval, handle_get_binding, handle_get_contract_version, handle_get_flow, handle_get_flow_version, handle_get_implementation, handle_get_repair_view, handle_get_run, handle_get_slot, handle_grant_standing_approval, handle_issue_contract_version, handle_list_records, handle_propose_binding, handle_prove_flow_version, handle_read_fixture_file, handle_read_spooled_file, handle_release_run, handle_resolve_unknown_outcome, handle_resume_run, handle_revoke_standing_approval, handle_roll_back_slot, handle_start_run, handle_submit_implementation and handle_try_implementation — with the Actor and the validated request, encode its answer as the tool result — values as JSON text, file bytes as base64 — and turn any exception the handler raises into a refusal answer through translate_failure, except any failure translate_failure answers internal_error — StopRequiredError, StoreInternalError or any unexpected exception, whatever the handler — which it lets propagate to serve_kernel unchanged, since a store change may already be written and only the next start derives every run again.

A tools/call that reached its operation returns the result {content: [{type: "text", text: T}], isError: B}: T is the answer of the operation as JSON text and B false, or T is the RefusalAnswer as the JSON object {code, reason} and B true for every refusal decided once the operation is known — fit, bounds, canonical form, permission, or translate_failure of an exception the handler raised; every refusal code is a member of = models.RefusalCode.
judgement.divergence: One implementation propagates an internal_error handler exception unchanged to serve_kernel, which sends an internal-error response and terminates the process; another returns it as a tools/call result with isError true and continues serving. The caller observes the different response shape, and the owner observes whether the kernel stops.
judgement.why: The exception rule requires propagation for every translated internal_error, while the return-shape rule includes translated handler exceptions among the refusals returned as tools/call results.

topics.topic: Whether invalid notifications/responses produce a refusal or always return empty bytes
questions: Must an oversized or unauthenticated notification/response produce the first-failure refusal required before parsing, or must every notification/response return empty bytes?

quotes: MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record; for tools/call, the message names a catalogue operation and fits that operation's request model with no unknown field — a field typed X | None fitting when it is absent or JSON null — and every bound below, else invalid_request; the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else not_permitted; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1).
The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.

A JSON object whose jsonrpc is "2.0" with a string method and an id is a request; one with a method and no id is a notification and one with no method a response: both are answered with empty bytes and change nothing.
judgement.why: Size and authentication are checked before the body is read and classified, so an oversized or unauthenticated body receives the corresponding refusal; empty bytes apply only after a successfully size-checked and authenticated body is recognized as a notification or response.
